name: Competitive dynamics model
purpose: Will a rival attack or respond?

parts.label: 2. Drivers of behaviour (AMA)
points: Awareness – blind spots: sudden change, routines, success

apply: Go through market & resource similarity, then A, M, A
Conclude on likelihood and timing of response
example: Apple vs Samsung (smartphones), Apple vs Microsoft (operating systems).

name: First-mover (dis)advantages
purpose: Is it better to move first or to be a fast second?

parts.label: When
points: Not in slow-cycle markets → fast second

name: Interactive strategies on price & quality
purpose: How do competitive moves shift customer expectations?

parts.label: Players
points: D = differentiating, M = mid-point, L = cost-leading, U = uncompetitive

parts.label: Dynamics
points: D raises quality at same price → new value line; M and L must adapt
M cuts price at same quality → next value line; L and D must adapt
Laggards fall below the line → U

name: Velocity of markets
purpose: How long can an advantage be protected?

parts.label: Slow-cycle
points: High barriers: fixed costs, complex processes, patents, history

parts.label: Fast-cycle
points: Advantage from adaptation (exploration, awareness, flexibility) and quickness
